endpoint.definition: A published address for one context space's data, with its own rules about who may read which entities and attributes.
endpoint.example: The public endpoint of the air-quality space answers anyone; an internal one answers your organization only.

policy.definition: The rule behind an endpoint: which operations a caller may perform, on which entity types, and which attributes come back.
policy.example: Anyone may read AirQualityObserved, without the attribute stationNote.

contextSpace.definition: Where one project's live data is kept, apart from every other project's; endpoints publish it and pipelines fill it.
contextSpace.example: The space air-quality holds the city's stations and their readings.

lane.definition: How much review a change needs before it happens: green goes through by itself, yellow needs a domain approval, red needs several people.
lane.example: Renaming a dashboard is green; publishing an endpoint to everyone is red.

change.definition: A proposed edit to the configuration, recorded so a person can read it and approve it before anything in service moves.
change.example: Add the endpoint public-air, proposed by a steward and approved by an administrator.

entityType.definition: The kind of thing an entity is, such as a station or a bus; the space's data model says which attributes each type has.
entityType.example: AirQualityObserved is the entity type of one air-quality reading.

ngsiLd.definition: The open standard (ETSI) the platform stores and serves context data in: entities with attributes, each attribute with its value and when it was observed.
ngsiLd.example: GET /ngsi-ld/v1/entities?type=Vehicle lists the buses an endpoint publishes.

linkml.definition: The language a data model is written in: classes, their attributes, units and allowed values. The Model editor writes it for you.
linkml.example: A class Station with the attributes name and location.

home.title: Home
home.purpose: Where you start: what you can do next in your projects, and what you visited lately.
home.one: Pick a project, or follow the first-run steps if you are new.
home.two: Open a recent or starred page to carry on where you left off.
home.three: Press Ctrl+K to find any page, space or resource by name.

organization.title: Organization
organization.purpose: The settings, people, groups and roles of the whole organization, for its administrators.
organization.one: Invite people and put them in groups.
organization.two: Give a group a role in the organization or in a project.
organization.three: Check the organization's limits and the health of its configuration.

spaces.title: Context spaces
spaces.purpose: A context space holds the data of one topic, such as air quality, as entities of the types its data model defines.
spaces.one: Create a space and give it a data model.
spaces.two: Bring data in with a pipeline or by loading a file.
spaces.three: Look inside a space to read, filter and correct its entities.

models.title: Data models
models.purpose: A data model says which entity types a space holds and what attributes each type has.
models.one: Start from a Smart Data Models type or write your own.
models.two: Add attributes with their type, unit and whether they are required.
models.three: Propose the model; pipelines then check their data against it.

datasources.title: Data sources
datasources.purpose: A data source is where data comes from: a web address, a CKAN dataset, an MQTT broker, a GTFS feed.
datasources.one: Add a source from a template, or fill in its address.
datasources.two: Store any password as a secret reference, never in the form.
datasources.three: Check the source: the Portal fetches it once and shows a sample.

pipelines.title: Pipelines
pipelines.purpose: A pipeline reads a data source on a schedule, maps each record and writes the entities into a space.
pipelines.one: Pick the source and the space it writes to.
pipelines.two: Map the fields to the entity type's attributes.
pipelines.three: Test it on a sample, then propose it; an approver starts it.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.purpose: An endpoint opens a space to the people and applications that read it, as NGSI-LD, GeoJSON, CSV and more.
endpoints.one: Choose the space, the representations and who may read it.
endpoints.two: Try it in the browser and copy the request as curl.
endpoints.three: Propose it; a public endpoint needs a publisher's approval.

policies.title: Policies
policies.purpose: A policy says who may read or write what in a space, down to types, attributes and areas.
policies.one: Pick the space and the person, group or application it applies to.
policies.two: Tick the operations and narrow them to types or attributes.
policies.three: Give it dates if it should end, and propose it.

ckan.title: Open-data catalogue
ckan.purpose: Publish a space's endpoint as a dataset in a CKAN catalogue, with its metadata and licence.
ckan.one: Connect the CKAN instance the organization publishes to.
ckan.two: Publish an endpoint as a dataset in one step.
ckan.three: Check what is published and keep it up to date.

dashboards.title: Dashboards
dashboards.purpose: A dashboard shows a space's data on maps, charts and tables that update by themselves.
dashboards.one: Create a dashboard and add a layer for each type to show.
dashboards.two: Choose how each layer looks: points, a heat map, a chart.
dashboards.three: Share the dashboard or place it in an application.

explore.title: Explore
explore.purpose: Look through an endpoint's data with filters and a map before you build anything on it.
explore.one: Pick a space and an endpoint you may read.
explore.two: Filter by type, attribute or area.
explore.three: Export what you see or copy a snippet to use the data elsewhere.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.purpose: Every change to a project waits here until an approver decides it; the history shows what was decided.
approvals.one: Open a change to read exactly what it would do.
approvals.two: Approve or reject it, with the name typed back for a risky one.
approvals.three: Read the history tab to see who decided what, and restore a removal.

activity.title: Activity
activity.purpose: What happened in the project: changes applied, pipeline runs, refused requests and more, newest first.
activity.one: Filter by kind, source or severity.
activity.two: Follow the live tail while you work.
activity.three: Open an event's object or change to see more.

assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.purpose: The assistant helps you build: it drafts resources and forms you review, and answers questions about the project.
assistant.one: Describe what you want in a sentence.
assistant.two: Review the draft it opens; nothing is saved until you propose it.
assistant.three: Approve changes yourself; the assistant never approves.

knowledge.title: Knowledge
knowledge.purpose: The pages and documents a knowledge assistant answers from, and where that assistant is placed.
knowledge.one: Add a website or a catalogue as a knowledge source.
knowledge.two: Crawl it and choose which pages to include.
knowledge.three: Place the assistant on your site or in the Portal.

workspaces.title: Copies
workspaces.purpose: A copy holds several changes together, so you can try them before bringing them back at once.
workspaces.one: Start a copy of the project.
workspaces.two: Make and test your changes in it; nothing is live.
workspaces.three: Bring it back as one change for an approver.

apps.title: Applications
apps.purpose: Applications built on the project's endpoints, generated by the assistant or built from the SDK.
apps.one: Generate an app by describing it, or open one that exists.
apps.two: Check it with real data in the preview.
apps.three: Publish it once the checklist is complete.

settings.title: Project settings
settings.purpose: The project's own settings: its members and their roles, its service accounts and its own access.
settings.one: Grant people and groups a role in the project.
settings.two: Create service accounts for programs that read or write it.
settings.three: See your own access and what each role allows.

conversations.title: Conversations
conversations.intro: What visitors asked the project's assistants and how each answer was made: the route, the searches, the tool calls and the model calls with their time, cost and the model's reasoning. Conversations are kept verbatim for 90 days, only passwords, tokens and card numbers are masked before a turn is stored; every read is recorded.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.lead: {organisation} wants everyone to be able to use this Portal and its open-data catalogue, including people who work only with a keyboard, a screen reader or magnification.

law.heading: Legal basis
law.body: This statement covers {host}. Accessibility is governed by Act No. 95/2019 Coll. on information technologies in public administration and Decree No. 78/2020 Coll. on standards for public administration information technologies, which take WCAG 2.1 level AA as the standard.

status.heading: Compliance status
status.body: This website is partially compliant with WCAG 2.1 level AA. The content listed below is not yet fully accessible.

gaps.heading: Content that is not accessible
gaps.maps: Maps show places only as a picture. The same places, with their addresses and coordinates, are in the dataset's table and in its download.
gaps.charts: Charts show numbers only as a picture. The same numbers are in the dataset's table and in its download.
gaps.screenReader: The test with the NVDA and VoiceOver screen readers has not been done yet; a screen reader may read some controls unclearly.
gaps.thirdParty: Other parties make the AI assistant window and the documents publishers upload (PDF, spreadsheets); we cannot vouch for their accessibility.

method.heading: How we checked
method.body: By self-assessment. The axe-core tool checks every page the Portal's automatic walk visits, in English and Slovak, at desktop and phone width, and the check fails on any serious or critical finding. We went through the five main journeys with a keyboard only.

dates.heading: Date
dates.body: This statement was prepared on {prepared} and last reviewed on {reviewed}.

contact.heading: Feedback and contact
contact.body: Did you meet a barrier? Tell us the page's address and what you tried to do.
contact.noEmail: This installation has not published a contact address yet; ask its operator, {organisation}.

enforcement.heading: Enforcement
enforcement.body: If our answer does not satisfy you, turn to the Ministry of Investments, Regional Development and Informatization of the Slovak Republic, which oversees the accessibility of public administration websites.
